result:
I'm staging this through the New-Project Entry. There's no spec, so the outcomes below come from your brief and need your confirmation. The three research reports are background only: they supplied facts and costs, not outcomes. Nothing goes into a roadmap file until you've ranked and confirmed.

## Candidate outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome | Source | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A real-time revision panel for total nonfarm: first, second and third print, preliminary and final benchmark, SA and NSA, by reference month | brief Part B | Small data volume (MBs): a few hundred months × ~5 vintages × 2 adjustments. The real cost is assembly. Vintage coverage depth isn't known until a probe runs. |
| O2 | Revision magnitude by stage over time (MAR, dispersion, tails), with 2003 and 2020–22 marked | brief Part A | Cheap once O1 exists: summary statistics only |
| O3 | SA one- and two-month revisions split into an NSA-sample part and a seasonal-factor part | brief Part C; all three reports call this the open gap | Needs O1's SA and NSA vintages. Compute is trivial if the split is an accounting identity, and measured by its stage if it's modeled. |
| O4 | The effect of collection days and first-closing rate on one-month revision scale | brief Part A §2 | Hand-built calendar covariate: one row per month, derivable from release dates. Collection-rate history depth isn't known until a probe runs. |
| O5 | A Bayesian multi-vintage state-space model for total nonfarm: latent path, news and noise per stage, Student-t measurement, stochastic volatility with covariates in log-scale, benchmark as an irregular precise observation with wedge-back | brief Part C | NUTS runtime can't be estimated without a fit. The core stage measures it. |
| O6 | Partial pooling of driver effects across NAICS supersectors | brief Part C | About 11× O1's data. Runtime is measured by the O5 stage and scales from there. |
| O7 | Hand-built capacity series (real appropriations, FTE, sample size), and their weakly identified effects on revision scale | brief Part A §3–5 | Your time: roughly 40 fiscal years from budget justifications and FedScope, one value per year per series. Likely days. |
| O8 | Explicit structural-change treatment (2003, 2020–22, redesigns), using change points or TVP with shrinkage | brief Part C | Measured by its stage: it adds parameters to O5 |
| O9 | Validation: targeted PPCs, LOO against a constant-variance baseline, pseudo-real-time checks | brief Part C | One baseline fit plus refits per pseudo-real-time origin. Multiplies O5's measured runtime. |

## Proposed tracks

- **A: Revision data and descriptives (O1, O2, O3, O4), known progression.** These are measurement-mechanics questions answerable without the full model. A first descriptive result shouldn't wait on the model's machinery. Please confirm you can name its stages first to last; if not, it becomes research.
- **B: Scale model (O5, O6, O8, O9), research.** The method is open. Only its core stage gets committed; the rest wait in a ranked list until O5 has run on real data.
- **C: Capacity covariates (O7), research.** Split from B for two reasons: it answers an institutional question with weak identification, and its data must be hand-built. Joined to B, the model would wait on that work.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 with uv, from `.python-version` and `uv.lock`.
- NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax if warranted, ArviZ and Polars, from the brief.

## Proposed probes

These need your yes before I run them:

- Fetch one real vintage set to firm up O1's coverage depth.
- Check that JAX and NumPyro wheels install under Python 3.14.

## Name

Proposed: `ces-revisions` → `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file by that name exists.

**One request:** rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves, and confirm or change the tracks, their kinds and the name. Say yes or no to the probes in the same reply.
